title: Croatian Government Scholarships in the academic year 2026/2027 (Bilateral Scholarships) — Scholarship B: Full undergraduate (BA) studies
legacy_titles: Scholarships of the Republic of Croatia
Bilateral Programme for Academic Mobility in Croatia
program_type: National government scholarship administered by ministry
administering_authority: Ministry of Science, Education and Youth of the Republic of Croatia
implementing_agency: Agency for Mobility and EU Programmes (AMPEU / Agencija za mobilnost i programe Europske unije)
programme_action: Croatian Government Scholarships (Bilateral Scholarships), Application Pool 1: Scholarships based on Bilateral Agreements, Scholarship type B — full degree BA/MA studies
description: The Ministry of Science, Education and Youth of the Republic of Croatia and the Agency for Mobility and EU Programmes (AMPEU) offer Croatian Government Scholarships in the academic year 2026/2027, known as Bilateral Scholarships. Scholarship B funds a full undergraduate (BA) degree at an accredited public Croatian higher education institution for a period of 36 or 48 months. For the 2026/2027 cycle the full-degree category is offered only under bilateral agreements with Hungary, Romania, the Slovak Republic and the People's Republic of China, and for the minority routes only to members of the Croatian national minority in those countries. Benefits comprise tuition-free full degree studies, monthly financial support, subsidised accommodation in student residence halls and subsidised meals in student restaurants.

programme_structure.allocation: Type B (full degree BA/MA) is allocated exclusively under valid/effective educational co-operation programmes and bilateral agreements with four sending countries: Hungary, Romania, the Slovak Republic and the People's Republic of China. The Croatian government allocates a fixed number of scholarships per country through the Joint Committee for Bilateral Scholarship Award.
programme_structure.quota: China: 8 scholarships for full degree undergraduate (BA), graduate (MA) or postgraduate (PhD) programmes (types B and C1). Romania: 2 scholarships for full degree programmes for members of the Croatian national minority in Romania (types B and C1). Slovak Republic: 5 scholarships for full degree programmes for members of the Croatian national minority in the Slovak Republic (types B and C1). Hungary: an unspecified number of scholarships for full degree programmes for members of the Croatian national minority in Hungary (types B and C1).
programme_structure.host_institutions: Accredited public Croatian higher education institutions only. Private Croatian higher education institutions and research institutes are not acceptable. The mobility cannot be carried out abroad.
award_categories: A1 — One semester study of the Croatian language (4–5 months)
A2 — Semester/partial Bachelor's or Master's studies (4–10 months)
B — Full undergraduate (BA) or graduate (MA) studies (BA: 36 or 48 months; MA: 24 or 12 months)
C1 — Full postgraduate doctoral (PhD) programme (36 months)
C2 — Partial postgraduate doctoral (PhD) studies or research for PhD students (1–10 months)
D — Postdoctoral studies and research (1–10 months)
E — Short postdoctoral research visit (3–29 days)
F — Summer seminar of Croatian language, literature and culture (2 weeks)
pools: Application Pool 1 — Scholarships based on Bilateral Agreements (open to citizens of 18 countries/territories; nomination by national competent authority required)
Application Pool 2 — Scholarships for learning the Croatian language (open regardless of bilateral agreement; nomination by current Croatian language professor)
programme_structure.bachelor_relevant_note: Application Pool 1 covers eligible sending countries Belgium (Flanders), Bulgaria, People's Republic of China, Czech Republic, Germany (Bavaria), Greece, Hungary, Israel, Italy, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Slovak Republic, Türkiye and Ukraine, but only Hungary, Romania, the Slovak Republic and China were offered Scholarship type B (full BA/MA) for this cycle.

status_note: The 2026/2027 Call for Applications closed on 10 April 2026 and the AMPEU online application system (www.ampeu.hr/scholarship_application/) now displays 'Prijave su zatvorene / Applications are closed'. Deadlines earlier than the verification date (2026-10-03) set the record to CLOSED. AMPEU publishes the annually recurring call on its Open Calls page, typically in February, with the call open during March and April for the following academic year; the next cycle (2027/2028) is therefore expected to open around February 2027 with a deadline around mid-April 2027.
verification_type: Direct review of the official 2026/2027 Call for Applications PDF plus the AMPEU Open Calls page, the AMPEU programme overview page, the Ministry of Science and Education publication page, and the live application portal.
verification_notes: All core facts — the Scholarship type B definition (full undergraduate BA degree, 36 or 48 months), the eligible sending countries, the benefits package, the 300.00 EUR monthly financial support, the 10 April 2026 deadline, the mobility window, and the eight required documents — were confirmed directly against the official 22-page Call for Applications PDF published at en.ampeu.hr and the AMPEU open-calls page. The record was verified against a closed cycle, so all dates reflect the 2026/2027 academic year.

application_deadline.typical_application_window: The call is published in February and remains open during March and April for the following academic year; the 2026/2027 call was created 20 February 2026 and closed 10 April 2026.
application_deadline.application_period: Published 20 February 2026; applications and nomination letters accepted until 10 April 2026.
application_deadline.official_rule: Deadline (Application Pool 1): the deadline for the candidates to submit their application documents in the Agency's online system and for the foreign partner institutions to send their Nomination Letters to the Agency by e-mail (preferably) or by post is the 10th of April 2026. Deadline (Application Pool 2): the deadline for the candidates to submit their application documents (including the Recommendation Letter) through the Agency's online application system is the 10th of April 2026.
application_deadline.deadline_warning: This deadline has passed (10 April 2026) and the online application system is closed. The stated deadline applies to both the applicant's online submission and the sending-country Nomination Letter; a nomination received after the deadline invalidates the application.

programme_duration.official_range: Full degree BA studies: 36 or 48 months. The country-specific allocations in the 2026/2027 Call state BA: 36 months.
programme_duration.renewal_note: A Bilateral Scholarship for a full cycle of undergraduate studies is granted for the full duration of the study programme but is renewed every year depending on academic success. The holder must submit each year proof of exams and ECTS credits obtained in the previous academic year and proof of enrolment in the next academic year. 35 or more ECTS credits: the scholarship is renewed. 34 or fewer ECTS credits: the scholarship is not renewed. Separately, students in full degree programmes must obtain 55 or more ECTS credits in the previous academic year to receive a full tuition fee waiver for the next year; students who obtain 30–54 ECTS credits must cover the cost of the unobtained ECTS credits (the difference between obtained credits and the maximum 60). Scholarship types B and C1 may not be extended beyond the awarded period.

funding.scholarship_type: Government bilateral mobility scholarship (tuition-free full degree + monthly financial support + subsidised accommodation and meals)
funding.monthly_amount_note: For undergraduate/graduate studies (scholarship types A1, A2 and B): 300,00 EUR monthly financial support, with July and August excluded. The Call states the monthly financial support is a contribution to living costs, not full coverage, and that holders must have sufficient funds for at least two months in Croatia. To receive the full monthly support the holder must be physically present in Croatia for at least 15 full uninterrupted days in that month.
funding.travel_amount_note: Travel expenses to Croatia and back to the country of origin are explicitly not covered by the scholarship package and are the responsibility of the scholarship holder. Applicants are advised to ask their sending institution whether it can cover travel costs.
funding.fully_funded_note: The award covers tuition and provides a monthly living contribution plus subsidised accommodation and meals, but it is not a fully funded award: travel to and from Croatia, visa-related fees and any other costs related to the stay in Croatia are not compensated, the monthly amount is a contribution rather than a full living allowance, and accommodation and meals are only subsidised, not free. The Call explicitly states that the monthly financial support is not meant to cover all costs of the scholarship holder.

tuition.conditions: Tuition-free full degree BA studies at a public Croatian higher education institution. The full tuition fee waiver for the next academic year is conditional on obtaining 55 or more ECTS credits in the previous academic year.

monthly_stipend.conditions: Monthly financial support for scholarship types A1, A2 and B; July and August excluded; at least 15 full interrupted days physically in Croatia per month required for full payment; paid only to a Croatian bank account opened by the scholarship holder.

travel_allowance.note: Travel expenses to Croatia and back are not covered and are the holder's responsibility.

visa_support.note: Visa and residence-permit costs are not compensated. Students coming for the purpose of studies are exempt from paying the visa fee. Third-country nationals must present a certificate of no criminal convictions.

insurance.note: EU nationals holding scholarship type B may transfer health care from their home country to Croatia under Regulation (EC) No 883/2004. Nationals of countries with social security agreements with Croatia (North Macedonia, Montenegro, Türkiye) obtain a patient's certificate. Others must organise and cover health care themselves; the Agency covers health insurance expenses only if foreseen in a valid bilateral educational co-operation programme.

research_allowance.note: Not published in official source for Scholarship type B

accommodation_support.conditions: Subsidised accommodation in student residence halls. Students staying in residence halls in Zagreb and Rijeka must undergo a health examination in their home country and bring a filled-in Health Certificate/Form.

bond.note: No service bond or return-home obligation is published. Obligations are limited to submitting the signed Letter of Acceptance before the mobility starts, a Final Report within one month after the mobility ends, staying in Croatia throughout the programme (with justified absence up to three consecutive summer months for full degree studies), and returning any undue payment of financial support.

total_estimated_value.note: The Call publishes a monthly amount and benefit categories, not a total award value. A total value is not computed here.

coverage: Tuition-free full degree undergraduate (BA) studies for 36 or 48 months
Monthly financial support of 300.00 EUR (July and August excluded)
Subsidised accommodation in student residence halls
Possible preparatory academic year of Croatian language learning for holders whose Croatian is not yet sufficient
Permit to work through Student Service Centres while enrolled in full degree BA studies
coverage_limitations: Travel costs to and from Croatia are not covered and must be paid by the student.
Visa fees, residence permit costs and other costs related to the stay in Croatia are not compensated.
The 300.00 EUR monthly amount is a contribution to living costs, not a full living allowance; the Call advises holders to have sufficient funds for at least two months in Croatia.
No monthly payment is made for July and August, and a month is only fully paid if the holder is physically present in Croatia for at least 15 full uninterrupted days.
Accommodation and meals are subsidised, not free, and depend on availability of student residence places.
Health insurance is not universally provided; it must be transferred, covered by a bilateral social security agreement, or arranged and paid for by the holder.
The tuition fee waiver for the following academic year is conditional on obtaining 55 or more ECTS credits in the previous academic year.
The scholarship cannot be held concurrently with any other scholarship, grant, stipend or Erasmus+ funding for the same mobility period.

The exact benefit structure may differ from the figures published for this cycle: the AMPEU Bilateral Scholarships programme overview page still lists 1.600,00 HRK monthly financial support for undergraduate studies in Croatian kuna, which is inconsistent with the 300,00 EUR figure in the 2026/2027 Call PDF. The Call PDF is treated as the authoritative current source.
eligible_applicants: Members of the Croatian national minority in Hungary, Romania and the Slovak Republic
Citizens of the People's Republic of China
Candidates who have completed a four-year high school degree (required for BA applications)
Candidates who secure a Letter of Invitation from the dean of a Croatian higher education institution and a provisional Enrolment Certificate for the desired BA programme

final_year_condition: Not applicable. This is an entry-level undergraduate award, so applicants must already hold a four-year high school degree at the time of application; final-year high school students who have not yet graduated are not eligible. The four-year high school degree must be accompanied by a request for recognition of the foreign secondary school qualification submitted to the Agency for Science and Higher Education together with the enrolment application.
equivalent_degree_note: Recognition of prior educational qualifications is an integral part of the enrolment procedure. Applicants to undergraduate (BA) study programmes who hold a foreign secondary school qualification must submit a request for recognition to the Agency for Science and Higher Education along with the enrolment application; forms and instructions are published on that Agency's website. Recognition may also be performed by the Croatian higher education institution.

age_limit.official_source: Candidates must be at least 18 years of age on the 1st of October 2026. Age limit of 30 years applies when applying for scholarships for full degree BA and MA study programmes (scholarship type B) and for full degree PhD programmes (type C1).

nationality_quota: Scholarship type B is offered only under bilateral agreements with Hungary, Romania, the Slovak Republic and the People's Republic of China. For the 2026/2027 cycle the full-degree quotas were: China 8, Romania 2, Slovak Republic 5 and Hungary an unspecified number (all shared with scholarship type C1 for postgraduate study). Applications from students will have priority over applications from teachers, and preference is given to applicants with higher Croatian language competence.

eligibility.citizenship: Scholarship type B (full degree BA/MA) is restricted to members of the Croatian national minority in Hungary, Romania and the Slovak Republic and citizens of the People's Republic of China. Applications from candidates who are residents of the specified countries but do not hold their citizenship are not taken into consideration, and candidates without the citizenship of the nominating country are ineligible.
eligibility.residence_requirement: Candidates must be citizens (not merely residents) of a country with a valid/effective educational co-operation programme or bilateral agreement with Croatia. Foreign citizens with a residence permit in Croatia, or applying for one, are not eligible, and students already enrolled in a study programme in Croatia are not eligible. Candidates holding only Croatian citizenship are not eligible.
eligibility.age_limit: Minimum 18 years of age on 1 October 2026; maximum 30 years for scholarship type B (full degree BA/MA studies).
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: A four-year high school degree is required when applying for BA studies.
eligibility.academic_requirements: Candidates must hold a four-year high school degree. Priority fields of study for types B and C1 include but are not limited to Croatian language and literature (Croatistika), Croatian culture and national identity (Kroatologija), History, Geography, Ethnology and Cultural Anthropology and Teacher Education Studies.
eligibility.language_requirement: A minimum level of B1 according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is required. Scholarship type B is delivered in Croatian, and candidates can only apply for study programmes delivered in Croatian at accredited public Croatian higher education institutions; English-language programmes and programmes at private Croatian institutions are not acceptable. In selection, preference is given to applicants with a higher level of Croatian language competence.
eligibility.financial_need: Not a stated selection criterion; the Call notes only that holders must have sufficient personal funds for at least two months in Croatia.
eligibility.previous_scholarship_restriction: Applications from candidates who have already been beneficiaries of the Bilateral Scholarships in previous years will have a lower priority, and precedence is given to first-time applicants. The Bilateral Scholarship cannot be awarded concurrently with other scholarships, grants or stipends, and a holder may not hold more than one scholarship funded from the Croatian national budget (Bilateral Scholarships, CEEPUS, Croatian Central State Office for Croats Abroad) or receive Erasmus+ funding simultaneously.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: Students already enrolled in a study programme in Croatia are not eligible. The scholarship application and the admission application to a Croatian university are two separate procedures, and the scholarship for full degree studies is approved only upon successful enrolment at the desired institution.
eligibility.health_requirement: Foreign students who will use student accommodation in residence halls must undergo a health examination in their home country and bring a filled-in Health Certificate/Form. Third-country nationals must present a certificate of no criminal convictions issued by their home country to the Police.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Type B is open to study programmes delivered in Croatian at public Croatian institutions, with stated priority fields including Croatian language and literature, Croatian culture and national identity, History, Geography, Ethnology and Cultural Anthropology and Teacher Education Studies.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: The Call publishes no minimum grade, GPA or percentage requirement for Scholarship type B.

english_requirement.test_score_note: The Call requires 'proof of language proficiency in English or Croatian' for Scholarship type B but names no specific test and publishes no minimum score. The only language threshold stated in the Call is a minimum of B1 on the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, which applies to the Croatian-language programmes offered.
accepted_tests: Any recognised proof/certificate of proficiency in English or Croatian (the Call does not specify an accepted test list or minimum score)

language_of_instruction.language_note: The Call states that the language of instruction for scholarship types A1, A2, B, C1 and F is delivered in Croatian, while C2, D and E are delivered in Croatian or English. Candidates for type B can only apply for Croatian-language programmes at accredited public Croatian institutions; English study programmes are not formally acceptable. Holders whose Croatian is not sufficient are granted a scholarship for an initial academic year of learning Croatian followed by a final language exam that must be passed, otherwise the scholarship is automatically discontinued.

application_method.application_route: Two-stage nomination route: the candidate submits documents in the AMPEU online application system and the sending country's national competent authority submits a Nomination Letter to bilaterala@ampeu.hr (or by post to Frankopanska 26, 10 000 Zagreb). Self-nominated applications sent directly to the Agency, the Ministry or a host institution are not processed.

selection_process.decision_maker: The Joint Committee for Bilateral Scholarship Award of the Ministry and the Agency performs formal assessment and final selection. The final decision on the acceptance of individual candidates is made by the Croatian host institution.
selection_process.selection_type: Nomination-based two-stage selection: preliminary selection and ranking by the sending country's national competent authority, followed by formal assessment and final selection by the Ministry and the Agency.
possible_stages: Preliminary selection and ranking by the national competent authority in the country of origin (applications ranked by these offices take priority)

selection_process.weighting_note: The Call publishes no numeric or percentage weighting for any criterion. Assessment is qualitative (formal completeness, academic profile, proposal and motivation).
selection_process.results_timing: Results are communicated during June and/or July of the year of application (June/July 2026 for this cycle).
selection_process.scholarship_rank_note: Applications from candidates who have already been beneficiaries of the Bilateral Scholarships in previous years have a lower priority; precedence is given to first-time applicants. In selection, preference is given to applicants with a higher level of Croatian language competence. An appeal against the decision of the Joint Committee shall not be accepted.

degree_outcome.awarded_qualification: Bachelor's degree (university undergraduate degree) awarded by the Croatian public higher education institution at which the holder enrols
degree_outcome.typical_programme_length: 36 months (the country allocations for 2026/2027 state BA: 36 months; the type description allows 36 or 48 months)
possible_awards: Bachelor's (BA) degree at an accredited public Croatian higher education institution
degree_outcome.degree_note: Scholarship B funds enrolment in a full degree BA study programme, i.e. a complete degree from entry to graduation rather than an exchange or partial study period. A scholarship for full degree studies is approved only upon successful enrolment at the desired higher education institution, after the applicant submits proof of enrolment. Scholarship types B and C1 may not be extended beyond the awarded period. English-language and private-institution programmes are not acceptable for this award.
degree_outcome.credit_transfer: Recognition of prior educational qualifications is an integral part of the enrolment procedure. Applicants to BA programmes holding a foreign secondary school qualification must submit a recognition request to the Agency for Science and Higher Education with the enrolment application. Renewal of the scholarship and the tuition waiver depend on ECTS credits obtained per academic year.

student_rights_and_cost_protection.tuition_fee_for_recipients: Tuition-free full degree BA studies. To receive a full tuition fee waiver for the next academic year the student must obtain 55 or more ECTS credits in the previous academic year; students with 30–54 ECTS credits must cover the cost of the unobtained ECTS credits (difference between obtained credits and the maximum 60).
student_rights_and_cost_protection.application_fee_for_recipients: No application fee is published in the Call. Visa fees are not compensated, although students coming for the purpose of studies are exempt from paying the visa fee.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: Scholarship holders must email the Agency the signed Letter of Acceptance accepting the awarded Bilateral Scholarship at least one month before the beginning of the mobility, and must send a Final Report about the mobility within one month after its end using an online questionnaire. Holders must obtain an OIB and open a Croatian bank account and send the details to the Agency, since support can only be paid to a Croatian bank account.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: Subsidised accommodation in student residence halls and subsidised meals at student restaurants. Type B holders may work through Student Service Centres (only holders of types A2 and B can be employed as students).
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No bond or mandatory return-home service requirement is published. The holder must stay in Croatia throughout the programme (shorter absences such as 7 days are acceptable; absence is justified for three consecutive months during summer only for full degree studies) and may be suspended or have the grant reclaimed for unexplained absence from Croatia. The holder is obliged to return any undue payment of financial support. The scholarship can be revoked due to poor academic performance or failing the final Croatian language exam after a preparatory year.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_breach_consequence: Unjustified departure from Croatia, failure to obtain the required ECTS credits, or failure to pass the Croatian language exam can lead to suspension, termination, automatic discontinuation or reclaiming of the grant.

programme_comparison_fields.recipient_countries: Hungary, Romania, Slovak Republic, China (type B only)

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: The Letter of Interest must be 1–2 pages. The Call's stated priority fields are Croatian language and literature (Kroatistika), Croatian culture and national identity (Kroatologija), History, Geography, Ethnology and Cultural Anthropology and Teacher Education Studies, so the letter should link the chosen BA programme to one of these fields, to Croatian-language competence, and to the applicant's membership of the Croatian national minority where relevant. It should also state the intended mobility period, since applicants must indicate a preferred mobility period that begins no earlier than 28 September 2026 and is completed by 30 September 2027.

risk_flags.risk: Eligibility for Scholarship type B is narrow: only Croatian national minority members in Hungary, Romania and Slovakia and Chinese citizens may apply, and only where a bilateral agreement is in force.
risk_flags.impact: Most European and international applicants are excluded from the full BA degree category.
risk_flags.mitigation: Applicants from other Pool 1 countries should consider scholarship types A1, A2, C2, D, E or F, which are offered to a wider list of 18 countries but do not fund a full bachelor's degree.

risk_flags.risk: Award depends on two independent approvals: nomination by the national authority and acceptance by the Croatian host institution.
risk_flags.impact: A complete online submission can still fail if the Nomination Letter is late or the host institution declines.
risk_flags.mitigation: Contact the national competent authority and the Croatian institution early; obtain the dean's Letter of Invitation and the provisional Enrolment Certificate as soon as possible.

risk_flags.risk: Financial support is partial: 300 EUR per month excluding July and August, with travel, visa, residence permit and health insurance costs not covered.
risk_flags.impact: Holders must finance travel, documents and summer months themselves.
risk_flags.mitigation: Budget for at least two months of living costs plus travel and visa costs, as the Call explicitly advises.

risk_flags.risk: Annual renewal is conditional on academic performance (35+ ECTS to renew; 55+ ECTS to keep the full tuition waiver).
risk_flags.impact: A weak first year can end the scholarship or create a partial tuition liability.
risk_flags.mitigation: Track ECTS accumulation each academic year and submit the renewal proofs (ECTS certificate and enrolment certificate) on time.

risk_flags.risk: Study is delivered in Croatian, and a preparatory language year ends in a final exam that must be passed.
risk_flags.impact: Insufficient Croatian can lead to automatic discontinuation of the scholarship.
risk_flags.mitigation: Prepare to at least B1 CEFR before applying and treat the preparatory year as a conditional pathway, not an entitlement.

risk_flags.risk: The AMPEU programme overview page still shows the monthly allowance as 1.600,00 HRK while the Call PDF states 300,00 EUR.
risk_flags.impact: Applicants may rely on an outdated or miscalculated figure from the general programme page.
risk_flags.mitigation: Use the cycle-specific Call for Applications PDF as the authoritative source and verify any figure with bilaterala@ampeu.hr.

risk_flags.risk: Concurrent funding is prohibited, including other scholarships funded from the Croatian state budget.
risk_flags.impact: Holding another stipend for the same mobility makes the holder ineligible.
risk_flags.mitigation: Declare and, if necessary, decline any other funding before accepting the Bilateral Scholarship.

database_notes: This record covers the assigned target: Croatian Government Scholarships in the academic year 2026/2027 (Bilateral Scholarships) of the Ministry of Science, Education and Youth and AMPEU, Scholarship B (full undergraduate BA studies), hosted in Croatia (Europe).
No substitution was made: the target is not on the RESEARCH_PROTOCOL do-not-duplicate list and its host region (Croatia, Europe) is allowed. It was recorded rather than substituted.

Region-scope note under the protocol: the award is hosted in an allowed region and a substantial share of its eligibility is not locked to a single excluded region, because Scholarship type B is open to members of the Croatian national minority in Hungary, Romania and the Slovak Republic as well as to citizens of China. Only the China route falls inside the protocol's East Asia exclusion scope, and it is documented as such; the three European minority routes are in scope. The wider Application Pool 1 country list is also predominantly European.

The cycle researched is 2026/2027 entry. Because the deadline of 10 April 2026 precedes the verification date of 2026-10-03, the record is set to CLOSED, with the next cycle expected around February to April 2027.

AMPEU publishes the call annually; its own programme overview page states that the Call for Applications is usually open during March and April for the next academic year, while the 2026/2027 call was actually created on 20 February 2026.

Amount inconsistency: the AMPEU Bilateral Scholarships programme overview page lists 1.600,00 HRK monthly financial support for undergraduate studies, whereas the 2026/2027 Call PDF lists 300,00 EUR. The Call PDF is treated as authoritative for this cycle and the discrepancy is recorded as a risk flag.

The AMPEU application portal URL has two variants in circulation: https://www.ampeu.hr/scholarship_application/ (used in the 2026/2027 Call and confirmed live, currently showing 'Applications are closed') and the Croatian-language entry point https://ampeu.hr/prijava_za_stipendiju/ used on the programme overview page. Both return HTTP 200.

The online Application Form on the AMPEU portal is completed in Croatian and is downloaded as a PDF; the applicant must keep a copy, and failure to receive the downloaded form means the application was not submitted.
No minimum GPA, percentage, IELTS/TOEFL/PTE/Duolingo score or interview is specified for this award, so those fields are null or false rather than estimated.

Age at application: the Call requires a minimum age of 18 on 1 October 2026 and a maximum age of 30 for scholarship type B. The age_calculation_date of 2026-10-01 is an approximation of the published 1 October 2026 reference date.

Admission and funding are separate procedures: the scholarship for full degree studies is approved only after successful enrolment at the chosen Croatian institution, and the final decision on acceptance of individual candidates is made by the Croatian host institution, not by the Ministry or AMPEU.

The nominal deadline includes two simultaneous conditions — the candidate's online submission and the sending authority's Nomination Letter, both by 10 April 2026. An application without a timely Nomination Letter is not processed.
Travel, visa and residence-permit costs are explicitly not compensated, so the award should not be presented as unconditionally fully funded.

No logo asset is published by the award owner specifically for this scholarship. The verified logo_url points to the AMPEU agency logo on AMPEU's own domain, since AMPEU administers the application; the Croatian ministry's own logo is available at https://mzo.gov.hr/img/govhr_logo.png if the database prefers the ministry mark.

The scholarship holder's Final Report obligation and the requirement to obtain an OIB and a Croatian bank account are recorded as post-award obligations because support can only be paid to a Croatian account.
